title: Recovery of representations from constant torsor pullbacks
statement: Let $V$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\ell$ a prime, $P$ a finite group and $c:Y\to V$ a finite etale $\operatorname{ULift}(P)$-torsor with nonempty connected total space [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Put $k=\mathbf F_\ell$ and $\widetilde k=\operatorname{ULift}(k)$.Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\widetilde k$-modules on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $A$ a $\widetilde k$-module, and suppose $c^*F\cong\underline A_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then there exists a $k$-representation $N$ of $P$ with $T_c(N)\cong F$ [def-weil-pbc-torsor-associated-module]. No finite generation is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0DV5 (3), 0DV6 and 0A3R, proof identifying the restricted representation; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS (gluing sheaves and mapping property), with module operations as in 0DV5 (3)

proof.text: Construct the representation N_F on F(Y) by restriction along inverse deck transformations, with scalars transported from ULift(k) to k. The one and multiplication laws are proved directly from the torsor action and presheaf functor laws in the defining module.

Obtain a normalized natural module morphism alpha from F to the coefficient-lifted equivariant section presheaf Q_F, using the constant torsor pullback. Apply bijectivity of normalized evaluation to every component; ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective and NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app turn alpha into a presheaf isomorphism.

Invert the presheaf isomorphism and apply presheafToSheaf. Q_F sheafifies to the explicitly defined associatedModuleFunctor evaluated on N_F. Compose with the invertible counit of sheafification at F to obtain the required isomorphism T_c(N_F) to F.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0DV5 (3), 0DV6 and 0A3R, proof identifying the restricted representation; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS (gluing sheaves and mapping property), with module operations as in 0DV5 (3); explicit section-evaluation implementation of the fixed-torsor argument
proof_origin.note: Canonical section representation constructed without any existence choice; evaluation and its gluing bijectivity split into independent strictly partial statements. The final presheaf inversion, sheafification and counit composition are proved in Lean.

theorem Scheme.GaloisCover.associatedModuleFunctor_essentialImage
    {V : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace V] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (P : Type u) [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V) [ConnectedSpace c.P]
    (F : Sheaf V.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))))
    (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))
    (h : Nonempty ((c.π)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))].obj F ≅
      (constantSheaf c.P.smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))).obj A)) :
    ∃ N : Rep.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ) P, Nonempty ((c.associatedModuleFunctor ℓ).obj N ≅ F)
